## Purpose

This SOP describes the acidification, trace metal preservation, and
digestion protocols for aqueous environmental samples prior to Inductively
Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) analysis. It covers dissolved
metals (filtration + acidification) and total recoverable metals (acid
digestion) [@usepa200_8].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Environmental water samples (surface water, groundwater,
  runoff, wastewater) requiring dissolved or total recoverable metals
  analysis by ICP-MS.
- **Does not apply to:** Solid matrices (soils, sediments, tissues), total
  metals by XRF, or organic analyte preparation.
- **Location:** Environmental analysis laboratories.


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report deviations          |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Definitions

- **Acid digestion (water samples):** The addition of concentrated
  HNO~3~ (typically 0.5--2% v/v final) to preserved water samples to
  dissolve any particulate metal and stabilize dissolved metals; a
  prerequisite for ICP-MS analysis [@usepa200_8].
- **Blank (method blank):** A reagent water sample carried through the
  entire preparation procedure; used to assess and correct for metal
  contamination introduced during sample processing [@apha2012].
- **Certified reference material (CRM):** A water sample with certified
  metal concentrations from an accredited producer (e.g., NIST, USGS);
  used to verify ICP-MS accuracy [@beauchemin2017].
- **Digestion blank:** A solution containing only the acid reagents (no
  sample) processed through the digestion procedure; detects
  contamination from reagents and vessels.
- **ICP-MS (Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry):** An
  analytical technique that vaporizes and ionizes a sample in an argon
  plasma and separates ions by mass-to-charge ratio to identify and
  quantify elements at parts-per-trillion concentrations
  [@beauchemin2017].
- **Method detection limit (MDL):** The minimum concentration of an
  analyte that can be detected with 99% confidence that the true
  concentration is greater than zero; determined from replicate blank
  analyses per 40 CFR Part 136 [@usepa200_8].
- **Preservation (acidification):** Addition of HNO~3~ to a water
  sample at the time of collection to prevent metal adsorption to
  container walls and to maintain dissolved metals in solution; required
  for regulatory compliance samples [@usepa200_8].
- **Relative percent difference (RPD):** |A - B| / ((A + B) / 2) × 100;
  used to assess duplicate precision; acceptance criterion is RPD ≤ 20%
  for environmental matrices [@usepa200_8].
- **Spike recovery:** The percentage of a known added concentration of a
  metal that is measured by the instrument; acceptable range is typically
  85--115%; used to check for matrix interferences [@usepa200_8].
- **Total recoverable metals:** Metals determined in an unfiltered sample
  after acid digestion; includes both dissolved and particulate-bound
  fractions [@usepa200_8].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical burns and corrosive vapors:** Concentrated nitric acid
  (HNO~3~, 67--70%) is an extremely corrosive oxidizing agent. Contact
  causes severe chemical burns. Vapors are highly damaging to respiratory
  tissue.
- **Hydrochloric acid:** Concentrated HCl produces corrosive fumes and
  can cause burns on contact.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### Engineering Controls
All acid dispensing, sample acidification, and hot block heating must be
performed inside an active chemical fume hood.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses or face shield
- [ ] Laboratory coat
- [ ] Acid-resistant nitrile gloves (double-gloving recommended)

### Emergency Procedures

In case of acid spill or chemical burn, refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) or call
campus safety. For acid contact with skin or eyes, flush immediately with
water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                              | Notes                                    |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Automated sample digestion block  | Hot block, programmable to 85--95 °C     |
| Chemical fume hood                | Required for all acid work               |
| Analytical balance                | If gravimetric volume verification is needed |

### Reagents and Consumables

| Item                              | Notes                                    |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Nitric acid (HNO~3~)             | Ultra-pure, trace metal grade            |
| Hydrochloric acid (HCl)          | Trace metal grade; used when target analytes include Ag, Sb, or high Fe [@usepa200_8] |
| Certified metal-free membrane filters | 0.45 µm DigiFILTERS or syringe filters |
| Metal-free polypropylene tubes    | 15 mL or 50 mL autosampler tubes         |
| Ribbed watch glasses or reflux caps | To prevent evaporation loss during digestion |
| Narrow-range pH strips            | To verify pH < 2                         |
| High-purity DI water              | For volume adjustment and blanks         |
| Multi-element stock solution      | Certified reference material for LFB spikes [@beauchemin2017] |


## Procedure

### Sample Preservation and Dissolved Metals Fraction

1. **Filtration:** Filter the raw, unacidified sample immediately upon
   collection or arrival through a certified 0.45 µm metal-free membrane
   filter. Discard the first 5 mL of filtrate to rinse the filter matrix.
   Collect remaining filtrate into a clean polypropylene tube.

2. **Acidification:** Add high-purity trace metal grade HNO~3~ dropwise
   to the sample container to achieve a final matrix concentration of 2%
   (v/v). For example, add 1.0 mL concentrated HNO~3~ per 50 mL sample
   matrix [@usepa200_8].

3. Verify pH is < 2 using a narrow-range pH strip. Store acidified
   samples for at least 16 hours prior to analysis to ensure proper metal
   desorption from container walls [@usepa200_8].

### Total Recoverable Metals Digestion (Hot Block)

1. Transfer a well-mixed 50.0 mL portion of unfiltered sample into a
   clean digestion tube.

2. Working inside a fume hood, add 1.0 mL of trace metal grade HNO~3~
   and 0.5 mL of trace metal grade HCl [@usepa200_8].

3. Place the digestion tube into the hot block. Fit with a ribbed watch
   glass or vapor reflux cap to prevent evaporation loss.

4. Program the block heater to 85--95 °C. Heat the sample for 2 hours
   without allowing the solution to boil [@usepa3015a].

5. Remove from heat, allow to cool to room temperature, and adjust back
   to the original 50.0 mL volume mark using high-purity DI water. If
   visible particulates remain, filter the digestate to prevent ICP-MS
   nebulizer clogging.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Avoiding Boil-Over
Monitor samples during the first 15--20 minutes of heating. If the
solution begins to bump or boil, reduce the block temperature by 5 °C.
Loss of sample volume through boiling invalidates the digestion
[@usepa3015a].
:::

### Shutdown and Cleanup

1. Allow the hot block to cool before removing tubes.
2. Rinse all non-disposable glassware and equipment with 10% (v/v)
   HNO~3~ followed by three rinses of DI water.
3. Dispose of acid waste per §8 below.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

| QC Element                          | Requirement                            |
|:------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------|
| Method blank                        | Process 50 mL DI water through full procedure; analyte concentrations must be below the MDL [@usepa200_8] |
| Laboratory fortified blank (LFB)    | Spike multi-element stock into DI water and carry through digestion; recovery must be 85--115% [@usepa200_8] |
| Laboratory fortified matrix (LFM)   | Spike a field sample; recovery 70--130% [@apha2012] |
| Duplicate samples                   | RPD ≤ 20% [@usepa200_8]               |
| Calibration verification            | Initial and continuing calibration per instrument SOP |

See @usepa200_8 and @apha2012 for additional QC guidance.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type              | Container                    | Disposal Method          |
|:------------------------|:-----------------------------|:-------------------------|
| Acid-preserved samples  | Acid waste carboy            | EH&S pickup              |
| Spent acid rinses       | Acid waste carboy            | EH&S pickup              |
| Used filters            | Solid chemical waste         | Standard hazardous waste |
| Empty acid bottles      | Triple-rinsed, labels defaced | Glass recycling          |


## Maintenance

- **Each use:** Wipe down the hot block surface and fume hood sill after
  acid work.
- **Monthly:** Inspect digestion tubes for etching or discoloration;
  replace as needed.
- **As needed:** Replace pH strips and membrane filters before expiration
  dates.

## Training Record

Training is documented in the lab training log. Before working
independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Observe a trained operator perform the procedure
3. Perform the procedure under supervision
4. Be signed off by the PI or designated trainer
